subject: Renewal: tiered multi-year + staged ramp + SLO credit trigger
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@nimbushealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal timing + projected capacity needs

Jonas —

We are starting to pull together our budget for 2027 and want to ring-fence capacity for our clinician‑facing triage product. Current run rate has been higher than forecasted (up ~45% q/q) and procurement asked that we lock a 2‑3 year commitment to secure pricing. Two asks:

1) Can Redwood provide a multi-year option with a staged ramp (we'll need about 2x capacity in Q1 then +50% by Q3)?
2) We need explicit language around auto‑renew opt‑out and a service credit if latency or SLOs degrade — procurement is sensitive to patient‑facing outages.

Copying Evan from procurement. Happy to share usage charts before EOD.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Product, Nimbus Health
agomez@nimbushealth.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Evan Patel <epatel@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + projected capacity needs

Alicia —

Thanks for the heads up and the context. We can absolutely model a 2–3 year commitment with a staged ramp. High level options I recommend we review on a call:

- Option A: 2‑yr locked term with annual true‑ups and a Q1 frontload (credits available if usage < committed).
- Option B: 3‑yr priced at a deeper discount with a defined ramp schedule (Q1 +100%, Q3 +50%), and a built‑in burst pool for seasonal spikes.
- Option C: 36‑month flexible term with annual rebaseline and an auto‑renew opt‑out window (60 days before renewal).

On SLOs: we can include a service credit ladder tied to monthly p99 latency and a latency‑triggered escalation path (credits scale at >X ms for >Y hours). I attached a draft deck and a proforma with modeled pricing for each scenario — see \"Nimbus_Renewal_Options_20260928.pdf\" and the pricing sheet.

I[0m (internal note: looping in Marissa for commercial cadence + Connor for ops sizing)

Would you be free for a 30‑minute call next week to walk the options?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0118

Jonas —

Procurement perspective / constraints:
- We prefer a co‑terming approach between two existing contracts (edgemodel + core inference) to simplify invoicing.
- Any auto‑renew must include an explicit opt‑out window and a pro‑rated unwinding mechanism.
- Service credit needs to be predictable: propose a set % credit per incident tier (we'll share our SLO targets).

Please send the commercial terms and an example of the credit ladder. Also confirm whether private deployment (VPC) affects pricing for the multi‑year discount.

Regards,
Evan Patel
Procurement Manager, Nimbus Health
procurement@nimbushealth.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Patel <procurement@nimbushealth.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + projected capacity needs

Evan — thanks; noted. A few clarifications:

- Co‑terming: we can co‑term multiple Redwood contracts into a single billing cadence, we just need the target co‑term date to size true‑up windows.
- Auto‑renew opt‑out: standard is 30–60 day window; for multi‑year deals we can push to 60 days. We'll add explicit pro‑rata unwind language.
- VPC pricing: private deployments typically reduce discounts due to infra+support costs; we will model both hosted and VPC pricing in the proforma.

Marissa — can you draft the commercial anchor (tiered commit + ramp schedule) and include the SLO credit ladder options? Connor — can you validate that the burst pool described (50% standby) is feasible for Q1 frontload?

Thanks,
Jonas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Evan Patel <procurement@nimbushealth.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 15:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + projected capacity needs

Evan / Alicia / team —

I've mocked up a commercial approach that balances Nimbus's risk appetite and Redwood's unit economics. Key points in the attached SOW & pricing proforma:

- Structure: 3‑year term with year 1 committed baseline = current run rate * 2 (frontloaded), year 2 increase +50%, year 3 +25% optional true‑up.
- Billing: co‑term all Redwood SKUs to 2029‑12‑31 with annual invoices and quarterly true‑up reviews.
- Auto‑renew: 60‑day opt‑out window; early termination allowed with a declining unwind schedule (12–3 months pro‑rata band).
- SLO credit ladder (proposal):
  * Tier 1: monthly p99 > 250ms for > 12 hours -> 5% credit on that month's invoice
  * Tier 2: monthly p99 > 400ms for > 6 hours -> 12% credit
  * Severe: partial or full downtime impacting >4 hours -> escalation & discretionary credits/replacement capacity

Operational notes: Connor confirmed the Q1 frontload is feasible if we reserve a burst pool (50% standby) and implement prefix/KV warming prior to the ramp. This will add a one‑time onboarding uplift and a small monthly reservation premium (detailed in the pricing tab).

Attaching: SOW‑staged‑ramp‑draft.docx + Redwood_Tiered_Pricing_Proforma.xlsx

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + projected capacity needs

Evan / Alicia —

Legal quick note on the draft: we can accept the 60‑day opt‑out and the tiered credit ladder as commercial remedies. Two asks from legal:

1) Replace open‑ended \"severe\" language with defined incident buckets and a maximum monthly credit cap (e.g., 25% of invoice month) to keep risk bounded.
2) Add a requirement for a joint post‑mortem within 5 business days for incidents that hit Tier 2 or above.

I'll circulate a short redline for the SOW by EOD Wednesday.

-Kim
